title: Help! question about: cJSON_Print
author: LittleProgrammer-L

comments.body:
The code looks good to me except that you leak `str` and don't abort in case `root == NULL`.

I tested it and it works fine. I will take a closer look.

`buffer` being `0` make absolutely no sense. This is a value on the stack, not a heap allocation. This is guaranteed to never be `0` though.

`buffer->buffer` being `NULL` is another matter entirely though. This means that the allocation failed.

And since you never checked if `string` is `NULL` it will print garbage in this case (or on most systems just SEGFAULT). You should really check `str` before passing it to `printf`!!

Thank you very much for your reply!

What I need to correct is that the way I put the printed result is via `cJSON_PrintUnformatted` function, I'm sorry to make this point misleading.

I think it should be the allocation of memory failure after I saw your answer, so I  find the file 'startup_stm32f303xe.s' and find the place where the stack is allocated:
`Heap_Size      EQU     0x200`    //0x00000200 equal 512 Byte
I change `0x200` to `0x400`, and all print results are normal.

What still make me confuse is that the allocation fails in the first two cases but doesn't in the third. 

Anyway, thank you very much for your reply~
Probably just the size. The parsed JSON is quite large, `sizeof(cJSON)` should be around 50 bytes or so.

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of why memory allocation is failing for certain JSON structures but not others
Guidance on proper error handling for cJSON functions
Information about memory requirements for parsing different JSON structures
Debugging approaches to identify memory allocation failures

_classification.category: Can be dockerized without any issue

dockerfile:
FROM ubuntu:20.04

# Avoid interactive prompts during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    && apt-get clean \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Clone the repository and checkout the specific commit
RUN git clone https://github.com/DaveGamble/cJSON.git . \
    && git checkout 2a087843e4f8b6bfae57d35621e3787e0b999a21

# Create build directory and build the project using CMake
RUN mkdir build \
    && cd build \
    && cmake .. \
    && make

# Set the default command to show where the build artifacts are located
CMD ["ls", "-la", "/app/build"]
